post.description: Lowers the stock by quantity (a whole number above zero, not above the position's stock; minimum and reserved stock are ignored), records it in the history and, in the same transaction, re-checks the product's orders. In-progress orders are respected; pending ones are walked oldest to newest, keeping each that fits entirely and cancelling the rest with reason 'INSUFFICIENT_STOCK: ...'. Requires ADMIN_WAREHOUSE.

201.description: Adjustment recorded; cancelled_orders lists the orders it cancelled

post.description: Registers a new vehicle in the fleet. Requires ADMIN_SYSTEM role.

get.description: Returns paginated users, optionally filtered by role and active status

post.description: Registers the remito and its position assignments atomically, incrementing stock (RN-04/05/06/07). A PROVIDER registers its own delivery: restock_order_id (one of its supplier's orders) is required, assignments are not allowed and supplier is its own, so the reception is created PENDING_LOCATION and adds no stock until an administrator assigns positions with PATCH.

400.description: PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND, ASSIGNMENT_QUANTITY_MISMATCH, RESTOCK_ORDER_PRODUCT_MISMATCH, SUPPLIER_REQUIRED, RESTOCK_ORDER_REQUIRED, ASSIGNMENTS_NOT_ALLOWED

403.description: PROVIDER_WITHOUT_SUPPLIER — provider not linked to a supplier

get.description: Paginated, filterable listing. Cancelled orders are hidden by default; pass includeCancelled=true to include them. A PROVIDER only sees its own supplier's orders: the supplier filter is forced to it.

parameters.name: includeCancelled
parameters.description: Include cancelled orders in the result (default false)

403.description: PROVIDER_WITHOUT_SUPPLIER — provider not linked to a supplier

post.description: Registers a request to a supplier. Never affects stock (RN-03). Accepts an optional expected_delivery_date (#134) that is informational only — it is not used in any stock computation.

400.description: INVALID_EXPECTED_DELIVERY_DATE — expected_delivery_date must be after now

post.description: Marks a pending restock order as cancelled. The order is kept as a historical record (soft delete). An order that already has receptions against it cannot be cancelled.

409.description: RESTOCK_ORDER_ALREADY_CANCELLED — the order was already cancelled; RESTOCK_ORDER_HAS_RECEPTIONS — receptions were registered against this order

400.description: Validation failed — field constraints not met

get.description: Returns paginated orders, optionally filtered by status, date range, or assigned vehicle

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled

post.description: Creates a new order and reserves stock. Supports Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate orders on network retries. Requires ADMIN_SALES, ADMIN_WAREHOUSE or OPERATOR role.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional idempotency key (UUID) to prevent duplicate order creation on network retries

400.description: DESTINATION_AREA_REQUIRED, ITEMS_REQUIRED, PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND, INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, QUANTITY_EXCEEDS_LIMIT, etc.

409.description: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_USER_MISMATCH, or IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS for a concurrent request

post.description: Cancels a pending order at once and restores reserved stock. An in_progress order stays in_progress with timestamps.cancellation_requested_at set until Infra reports it cancelled, once the vehicle has put the goods back; the change arrives over the WebSocket. ADMIN_WAREHOUSE and ADMIN_SALES may cancel any order, OPERATOR only the orders they requested.

200.description: Order cancelled, or its cancellation requested from Infra

403.description: Insufficient role, or ORDER_NOT_OWNED — an operator's order of someone else

post.description: Per calendar bucket (day, week or month), how many non-cancelled orders, order lines and units came from a recommendation (the optional from_recommendation flag of each item in POST /orders). Every bucket of the range is returned, empty ones with zeros. Filters restrict the lines considered.

200.description: One row per bucket, oldest first

post.description: Weighted daily demand and, per active product, whether to restock and how much. Every param is required: each team sends its own business decisions. Inventory position = available (already net of reservations) + on order.

200.description: One row per product, most urgent first

post.description: Computes every active product's restock recommendation with the given params and stores it on the product (product.restock), stamped with calculated_at. Called once a day by the restock-cron service. Filters are not accepted: a run always covers every product, so all recommendations share one calculation time.

200.description: The rows written, most urgent first

post.description: Returns chart-ready series. Rejects unknown or over-broad queries.
Status, battery and an optional error. Faults arrive here too, as `error`, instead of on a separate channel. The id in the path is Infra's; the first reading of an id creates the vehicle.
Infra confirms in_progress (with the vehicle that took the order), completed or cancelled. Repeating the current status is a no-op, so redelivery is safe.

Opens a text/event-stream. Body: subscriptions[] of {id, kind, ...params}; id matches [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64} and is unique; at most 200. Kinds: metric {metric, range, step, filters?, group_by?, agg} (as POST /metrics/query with range 5m|15m|1h|6h|24h instead of from/to), logs {service?, level?, request_id?, text?, range, limit?} (as POST /console/logs/query), ws-events {feed: orders|user-orders|vehicles|stock-alerts}, status {}. Events: snapshot (first frame of a subscription), update (mode replace for metric/status, append for logs/ws-events), error {id, code, message}, end {reason: token-expired | server-shutdown | limit}; data is {id, mode, data} with the REST payload. Heartbeat ': ping' every 15 s. At most 10 streams per user (the user's oldest is ended with limit when a new one exceeds that) and 50 in total.

429.description: STREAM_LIMIT: the global cap of open streams is reached

post.description: Filters: service (backend|bridge), level (debug|info|warn|error), request_id, text, from, to, limit (default 100, max 500). Range at most 7 days; defaults to the last hour. Lines are newest first; total is the number of returned lines.
Authenticate with email/password and receive a signed JWT token

200.description: Login successful — returns JWT and user info

400.description: MALFORMED_REQUEST — body is not valid JSON

post.description: Stores the file as <path>/<uuid>.<ext> and returns the URL and key. The optional `path` part is one segment of 1 to 64 letters, digits, '_' or '-' (default `images`); anything else is a 400 BAD_REQUEST. Requires ADMIN_WAREHOUSE, ADMIN_SALES or SUPERADMIN role.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Folder for the file: 1 to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; defaults to images

patch.description: Partial update — only provided fields are changed
Assigns warehouse positions to a reception that is in PENDING_LOCATION status.
Partial update — only provided fields are changed. Requires ADMIN_WAREHOUSE or ADMIN_SALES role.
Partially updates a vehicle's state (status, position, battery, etc.). All fields are optional — only provided fields are updated. Requires ADMIN_SYSTEM role.

Forces an order into the given status (in_progress, completed, or cancelled), simulating the asynchronous transition that would normally arrive via Kafka. Completing an order drains its stock. Reverting to pending is rejected, and orders already completed or cancelled cannot be modified.
Assigns a vehicle to a pending or in-progress order, transitioning it to IN_PROGRESS. Simulates the asynchronous assignment that would normally arrive via Kafka.

get.description: Includes quantity_received_so_far, computed from linked receptions. A PROVIDER only finds its own supplier's orders.

403.description: PROVIDER_WITHOUT_SUPPLIER — provider not linked to a supplier

get.description: Self-describing catalogue: each entity lists its queryable fields, their types and the operators each field permits. Mirrors GET /metrics/catalog.
Adjustments across all the product's positions, newest first. Requires ADMIN_WAREHOUSE or ADMIN_SALES.
Returns total stock and the positions where this product is stored
Returns the catalogue categories accepted by the API (RFC sec 3.3)

Self-describing catalogue: each entry carries the dimensions and aggregations a valid query may use, so a client can build a metric picker without further docs. computed_metrics lists the metrics the backend calculates, each with its endpoint and the params it requires.

get.summary: Recent WebSocket events of a feed
get.description: Newest first, at most 200. Feed is one of orders, user-orders, vehicles, stock-alerts.

State (UP|DOWN|UNKNOWN) of backend, bridge, mongodb, redpanda, minio, victoriametrics, victorialogs and otel-collector, probed in parallel. dev is true under the dev or docker profile. uptime_ms is set for the backend only.
SUPERADMIN only. Sorted by path then filename; capped at the first 1000 objects, with `truncated: true` when the bucket holds more.
